title: Vulvar Cancer FIGO 2021 Staging, SLNB & Radical Vulvectomy
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: FIGO Cancer Report 2021: Cancer of the Vulva
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Vulvar Cancer (2024)

steps.say: Vulvar squamous cell carcinoma arises via two biologically and clinically disparate oncogenic pathways. HPV dependent lesions affect younger women while lichen sclerosus drives differentiated VIN in elderly patients.
steps.tx: Vulvar squamous cell carcinoma arises via two **vulvar SCC pathways**: **HPV-associated (uVIN, p16 positive)** driven by HPV **16** in younger women (**30** to **40** percent of cases), and **HPV-independent (dVIN, TP53 mutated, lichen sclerosus)** arising from chronic lichen sclerosus in women aged **60** to **70** with mutated p**53**.

steps.say: Accurate measurement of stromal invasion depth determines whether inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy is indicated. Depth is measured from the adjacent dermal papilla to the deepest invasive front.
steps.tx: Standardized **depth of invasion measurement** measures from the epithelial-stromal junction of the adjacent **superficial dermal papilla** to the deepest tumor cell nest. In **Stage IA <=2 cm invasion <=1.0 mm** (tumor diameter <=**2** cm, invasion depth <=**1.0 mm**), nodal metastasis is <1 percent, permitting safe **omission of groin dissection**.

left.title: Stage IA Microinvasive (Invasion <=1.0 mm)
points: Tumor diameter <=2 cm, stromal invasion <=1.0 mm
Radical local excision alone; omit groin lymphadenectomy

right.title: Stage IB Invasive (Invasion >1.0 mm)
points: Tumor diameter >2 cm OR stromal invasion depth >1.0 mm
Lymph node metastasis risk rises to 10% to 30%
Mandates inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy or sentinel node biopsy

steps.say: The updated FIGO 2021 staging system categorizes regional lymph node metastasis by number, size, and extracapsular extension. Nodal parameters directly allocate patients into Stage IIIA, IIIB, or IIIC.
steps.tx: In **FIGO 2021 Stage III nodal** staging: **IIIA 1-2 nodes** (metastasis in **1** or **2** lymph nodes <**5 mm cutoff**, or **1** node >=5 mm), **IIIB >=3 nodes** (**>=3** lymph node metastases <5 mm, or >=2 nodes >=5 mm), and **IIIC extracapsular extension** (any nodal metastasis displaying extracapsular spread through the node capsule).

rows: 1-2 nodes with metastasis <5 mm, or 1 node >=5 mm
Adjuvant groin/pelvic radiotherapy indicated if >1 node or >=5 mm
>=3 nodes with metastasis <5 mm, or >=2 nodes >=5 mm
Bilateral groin and pelvic external beam radiotherapy mandatory
Any nodal metastasis with extracapsular tumor spread
High risk of regional relapse; concurrent chemoradiation required

steps.say: Sentinel lymph node biopsy using technetium radiocolloid and blue dye has revolutionized surgical staging for early unifocal tumors. Groin dissection is avoided in node negative patients.
steps.tx: In the prospective **GROINSS-V** trial for **unifocal tumor <4 cm** with stromal invasion >**1** mm and clinically negative groins, **SLNB** utilizing technetium-**99**m radiocolloid and isosulfan blue dye identified sentinel nodes with >**95** percent sensitivity, delivering a marked **lymphedema reduction 40% to <10%** (**40** percent down to less than **10** percent).

nodes.label: Select unifocal vulvar tumor <4 cm with clinically negative groins
Identify radioactive and blue sentinel lymph nodes in inguinofemoral basins
Submit for serial ultrastaging: omit complete lymphadenectomy if negative

steps.say: Pathological evaluation of sentinel lymph nodes requires rigorous protocol sectioning combined with immunohistochemistry. Ultrastaging identifies subtle micrometastatic deposits.
steps.tx: **Pathologic ultrastaging** mandates **serial sectioning 50-100 um** (**50** to **100** um intervals) through the entire sentinel node combined with anti-**cytokeratin IHC** (AE**1**/AE**3**). This distinguishes macrometastases (>**2** mm) from **micrometastases** (>**0.2** to <=2 mm) and isolated tumor cells (<=0.2 mm or under **200** cells).

rows: Controversial; currently observed or managed individually

steps.say: The subsequent GROINSS V II trial investigated whether groin radiotherapy could replace completion lymphadenectomy in patients with micrometastatic sentinel nodes. Radiotherapy achieved outstanding regional control.
steps.tx: The phase II trial **GROINSS-V II** proved that in patients with **sentinel micrometastasis <=2 mm** (**2** mm or less without extracapsular spread), adjuvant **inguinofemoral radiotherapy 50 Gy** (**50** Gy) safely replaced completion groin lymphadenectomy, achieving a very low **groin recurrence 1.6%** (**1.6** percent) without severe lymphedema.

left.title: Sentinel Micrometastasis (<=2 mm, No ECE)
points: Inguinofemoral radiotherapy (50 Gy) is safe and effective
Avoids severe surgical lymphedema from complete groin dissection

right.title: Sentinel Macrometastasis (>2 mm or ECE)
points: Radiation alone carries unacceptable groin relapse rate (>25%)

steps.say: Contemporary surgical technique utilizes separate incision approaches rather than en bloc radical vulvectomy. Triple incision techniques substantially reduce operative wound breakdown.
steps.tx: Standard surgical execution utilizes the **triple incision technique** (one midline vulvar incision plus **separate groin incision** bilaterally), executing **radical local excision** with inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy. This approach eliminates the historical skin bridge and achieves a marked **reduced wound breakdown** rate (dropping dehiscence from 50 percent to 15 percent).

steps.say: Obtaining clear microscopic margins is essential to prevent local recurrence on the vulva. Formalin fixation induces tissue shrinkage requiring wider surgical clearance in the operating theater.
steps.tx: Securing an **8 mm fixed margin** on permanent formalin-fixed pathology represents the gold standard for **local recurrence prevention**. Because tissue contracts 20 to 25 percent upon formalin immersion, the surgeon must achieve an intraoperative **10-15 mm surgical margin** (**10** to **15** mm) around macroscopic tumor edges to secure pathological clearance.

rows: Surgical re-excision to achieve 8 mm if anatomically feasible
Re-excision or post-operative local external beam radiotherapy
